verdict.rationale: Portkey's gateway documents rule-based model switching. Availability-driven fallback is well covered: a prioritized provider/model list, triggers on non-2xx status codes, and circuit protection. Conditional routing to different targets based on custom checks and weighted load balancing are also documented. Cost-based routing appears only as a marketing mention of 'smart routing', and capability-based routing is only implied by generic conditional checks. Missing for 10: documented cost-threshold routing rules, documented capability-based model selection policies, evidence of policy-driven switching within a multi-step agent task, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my agent can switch models mid-task by policy — cost, capability, or availability — through gateway routing rules

citations.quote: If the primary LLM fails, Portkey automatically falls back to the next in line.
By default, fallback triggers on any **non-2xx** status code. Customize with `on_status_codes`
Route to different targets based on custom conditional checks
Set up granular cost tracking, intelligent caching, and smart routing to cut infrastructure spends without touching your application logic.
